summary: Working in philosophy and religious studies, René Guénon studied at the Robert-Badinter School Complex (1902–1903), Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1904–1906), and the University of Paris (1914–1917).

A scholar in Tibetology and religious studies, he studied at the University of Berlin, LSE, SOAS, and the University of Vienna under Wilhelm Koppers, Josef Haekel, Robert Bleichsteiner, Giuseppe Tucci, and Joseph Rock. He worked at Weltmuseum Wien in 1958.
Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Reting Rinpoche studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche and Chatral Sangye Dorje, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso.
An Indologist, Rewa Prasad Dwivedi studied at Banaras Hindu University, where he later served as Head of Sahityavidya from circa 1977 to 1995.

Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, Rewata Dhamma earned degrees including a doctorate from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1956 and 1967, and completed a doctorate at Banaras Hindu University (1956–1967).

Richard A. Hutch studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago in the field of religious studies. He held academic posts at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).
Working in Indology and Tibetology, Richard B. Martin served as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003) at the University of Virginia.

A Buddhist studies practitioner, Baker studied at UC Berkeley, Harvard, and under Shunryu Suzuki, whom he succeeded in 1971. He co-founded and served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center (1971–1984) and later founded Dharma Sangha.
Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Richard Barron studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and the 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

A scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, Bowring studied at the University of Cambridge. He held posts at Columbia and Princeton before becoming Professor of Japanese Studies at Cambridge (1985) and Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012).

An Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, Temple served in the Bengal Staff Corps and Indian Staff Corps. He edited The Indian Antiquary (1901) and was vice-president of the Hakluyt Society (~1928–1931).
Working in Indology and religious studies, Richard D. Mann earned his PhD at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003) and held a post at Carleton University (attested 2007).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Sinology, McBride earned his PhD at UCLA under mentor Robert Buswell. He held posts at Dongguk University and Brigham Young University (attested 2019).

An archaeologist who studied at the University of Bonn (~1895–1899), Delbrueck served as professor of archaeology at the University of Jena (~1918–1928) and held posts at the University of Bonn (~1928–1940) and University of Giessen (~1940–1945).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies, Richard F. Nance earned his PhD from the University of Chicago by 2004. He later served as Assistant Professor of South Asian Buddhism at Indiana University (attested 2013).

An Indologist, Fick earned his doctorate at Kiel University (1885–1888). He worked at Kiel University library, the Prussian State Library, and served as director of Göttingen State and University Library (1921–1932) and honorary professor at Göttingen (1923).

Specializing in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies, Foltz studied at the University of Utah and Harvard. He taught at Brown, Columbia, Kuwait, and Florida, and became Founding Director at Concordia University (~2007–2026).
Richard Fritzsche studied under Hermann Brockhaus from circa 1872 to 1876 and later served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg.

An Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, Gombrich studied at Oxford and under K. R. Norman, Walpola Rahula, and Gananath Obeyesekere. He served as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1976–2004) and president of the Pali Text Society (1994–2002).

Richard Hartshorne studied at Princeton University (~1917–1920) and the University of Chicago (~1921–1924). He held academic posts at the University of Minnesota (~1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1940–1970).
